title: Som Tam
subtitle: Thai green papaya salad with lime, fish sauce, and chilli
excerpt: Thailand's most beloved salad: shredded unripe green papaya pounded in a mortar with garlic, chilli, lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar into a sour, salty, sweet, and fiercely hot combination that wakes up every taste receptor at once.

recipe.sourceNotes: Som tam (sour pounded) is the most widely eaten dish in Thailand, sold at street stalls from early morning throughout the country. Its origins are in Isan, the northeastern region of Thailand, and in Laos, where it is called tam mak hoong; it has spread from there to become a staple across the country. The use of unripe green papaya as the base is the defining characteristic: the papaya provides crisp, slightly bitter flesh that absorbs the dressing without becoming soft. The technique involves pounding the ingredients in a large clay mortar, bruising rather than crushing them so the flavours meld but the texture remains crunchy. The balance of the dressing (sour lime, salty fish sauce, sweet palm sugar, hot chilli) should be adjusted to taste; Thai versions are significantly hotter and more pungent than most versions made outside Thailand.

recipeTools.notes: A large clay or stone mortar is essential for the bruising technique. A mixing bowl with a wooden spoon can approximate the result but the texture will differ.

content.text: Green papaya is available from Asian grocery stores; it should be rock hard and bright green inside, not yellow at all. Pound the garlic and chilli first to a paste, then add the other ingredients in the traditional order: the pounding bruises the papaya rather than turning it to mush. Taste and adjust the balance constantly; the four tastes (sour, salty, sweet, hot) should each be distinct but in balance.

content.text: In a large mortar, pound the garlic and chilli to a rough paste. Add the green beans and bruise them with a few strokes of the pestle without crushing completely.

Add the shredded papaya and tomato halves. Pound and turn with the pestle, using a spoon to keep the ingredients moving, for 1 to 2 minutes. Add the fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar. Pound and toss to combine. Taste and adjust: it should be simultaneously sour, salty, sweet, and hot.
Transfer to a plate. Scatter with crushed peanuts. Serve immediately with sticky rice or plain jasmine rice. The salad will not keep; eat it fresh.
